title: Regular branch and field intersection at a split nodal boundary point
statement: Let k be a field and f:X→Spec k a reduced finite-type scheme. Let i:Y→X be a reduced closed subscheme, with every irreducible component of X and Y of topological Krull dimension one [def-weil-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let y be closed in Y and suppose i(y) lies in the scheme-theoretic closure Z of X minus Y. Suppose the maximal-ideal completion of O_{X,i(y)} is isomorphic as a ring to κ(i(y))[[u,v]]/(uv) [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then O_{Y,y} is regular local, and for every t∈Y×_X Z mapping to y its local ring is a field [def-pc-fibre-product]. Neither global nodality nor separability over k is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: Finite type gives Noetherianity. The reduced-image theorem and complementary-component theorem identify Y and Z as complementary reduced unions. Boundary membership supplies an incident component in each union. At the closed point all incident components have local dimension one.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: Write A=O_{X,i(y)}, F=κ(i(y)), H=Â. The primes of H=F[[u,v]]/(uv) are (u),(v),(u,v): a prime contains u or v, and its image in the corresponding one-variable power-series local domain is zero or maximal. Faithful flatness gives a prime above each minimal prime of A; the maximal prime contracts to the maximal ideal, so at most two minimal primes occur. Boundary membership forces exactly two, p and q, one for each union. Both are nonzero.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: The local curve domains A/p and A/q have reduced dimension-one completions by the curve-normalization completion theorem. Quotient compatibility identifies these with H/pH and H/qH. Thus pH,qH are radical, their quotients have dimension one, and neither is zero by faithful-flat contraction. Radical ideals are intersections of their containing primes. The three-prime list leaves exactly the two distinct axes for pH,qH.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: Reducedness of the complementary component unions identifies the local closed-immersion ideals with p and q. The extended sum is the maximal ideal of H, so contraction gives p+q=m_A. The pullback local ring is A/(p+q), hence a field. The completion of the Y stalk is the axis quotient F[[t]], which is regular. Descent of regularity from completion gives regularity of the original stalk.

theorem split_nodal_boundary_local_rings
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsReduced X]
    (hX : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents X, topologicalKrullDim C = 1)
    (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsReduced Y]
    (hY : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents Y, topologicalKrullDim C = 1)
    (y : Y) (hy : IsClosed ({y} : Set Y))
    (hboundary : i y ∈ Set.range (Scheme.openComplementOfIsClosedImmersion i).ι.imageι)
    (hcompletion : Nonempty
      (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk (i y)))
        (X.presheaf.stalk (i y)) ≃+*
        (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) (X.residueField (i y)) ⧸
          Ideal.span {(MvPowerSeries.X 0 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2)
            (X.residueField (i y))) * MvPowerSeries.X 1}))) :
    IsRegularLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk y) ∧
      ∀ t : pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) i
          (Scheme.openComplementOfIsClosedImmersion i).ι.imageι,
        pullback.fst i (Scheme.openComplementOfIsClosedImmersion i).ι.imageι t = y →
        IsField ((pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) i
          (Scheme.openComplementOfIsClosedImmersion i).ι.imageι).presheaf.stalk t)
